Subject: Feature parity tests — tool calling & streaming next steps

Hi Liam / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion and clear priorities on your side. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the competitive/feature parity tests running: 

What we heard: 
- Primary objective: confirm parity vs hyperscaler APIs on structured outputs, tool/function calling reliability, and streaming latency under your query patterns.
- Success metrics: end-to-end P95 latency, token-level throughput, correctness of structured JSON outputs (schema pass rate), and function-call fidelity (name/arg accuracy).
- Constraints: 500-1,000 concurrent short-chat sessions and a subset of 10 heavy-long contexts (up to 2k tokens) for streaming tests.

Proposed next tests (short list):
1) Tool/function calling: run 1,000 scripted calls covering 20 function schemas from your catalog; measure call-matching and arg extraction.
2) Structured outputs: run our JSON-schema prompt suite and measure pass-rate + flaky examples.
3) Streaming: compare token latency (first-byte and tail) across Redwood hosted endpoint vs your current hyperscaler endpoint (we'll provide streaming client).
4) Side-by-side: if you want, we can run a 72-hour Dedicated instance on our end to mirror peak load and collect KPIs.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.pdf (MAP) — includes timeline, responsibilities, and proposed test harness schedule.

Next steps I suggest:
- You confirm which test buckets to prioritize (tool-calls / streaming / structured).
- We provision a short-lived Dedicated instance if you want a side-by-side.
- We share the test harness and a Drive folder (links below) so your SRE/QA can run locally or let us run.

Links: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c-acme-testing
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2026-41

Happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow to align.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and MAP. This is exactly the kind of structured approach we needed. Quick questions before we lock the plan: 

1) For streaming, can you confirm the metrics you capture on the client vs server (first-byte, token gaps, rebuffering events)? We need both client-observed and server-observed metrics to reconcile our dashboards.
2) For function calling: how do you handle ambiguous arg mapping? In our previous evals with another vendor we saw different heuristics that produced mismatches on nested arg objects.
3) Will you provide the harness or do we run locally? Our SRE team is happy to run locally but it helps if we can compare identical logs.

We want to prioritize tool/function calling and streaming first. If you can share the harness and a short runbook for schema instrumentation, we'll kick off next week.

—Liam

Head of AI Platforms, Acme Corp
liam.oconnor@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@acme.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feature parity tests — tool calling & streaming next steps

Liam —

Great questions — answering inline and dropping the harness link below.

1) Streaming metrics: we capture server-side: first_byte_ms, inter_token_gap_ms (per-token histogram), server_send_rate_tps, queue_depth. Client-side: client_first_byte_ms, total_rtt_ms, rebuffer_events, dropped_frames (where applicable for streaming audio). We export both as JSONL logs so you can join by request_id (we recommend instrumenting request_id in the client).

2) Function calling ambiguity: our runtime uses a two-stage matcher — intent->candidate functions (LLM disambiguation) + deterministic arg-normalizer (schema-first canonicalizer). For nested objects we provide a path-based validation and a confidence score. The harness produces a per-call report: matched_function, normalized_args (JSON), match_confidence, and failure_reason when below threshold. We'll include a config flag to force strict-schema enforcement for your tests.

3) Harness/runbook: we attached acme-test-harness.zip (contains a Python test runner, streaming client example, and schema instrumentation hooks). Drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c-acme-testing

I've also attached a small sample CSV with our baseline metrics vs GCP Vertex and AWS Bedrock for a handful of prompts so you have a reference (redwood-vs-hyperscaler-metrics.csv). Those are synthetic but useful to set expectations.

Proposed timing: your SRE runs the harness against your hyperscaler endpoint and our hosted endpoint this week; if you'd like a dedicated side-by-side, Ben can scope a 72-hour Dedicated run. Suggest a sync on Thursday to review results.

If you want, Ben can also provide suggested runtime/configs for streaming (max inflight tokens, chunk size, heartbeat).

Thanks — I put the action items in the MAP.

Best,
Marissa

--
Attachments: acme-test-harness.zip, redwood-vs-hyperscaler-metrics.csv

Subject: Re: Feature parity tests — tool calling & streaming next steps

Hi all —

Looping in some quick configuration guidance from an infra perspective in case you run the side-by-side Dedicated test: 

- Streaming: recommend chunk_size=64 tokens, max_inflight_requests=8 per connection for your short-chat workload; this balances first-byte latency vs throughput.
- KV-cache: enable prefix sharing for repeated system prompts to reduce redundant token compute; we can set TTL=300s for your cache during the 72-hour run.
- Function calling throughput: for parallel function invocations, keep batch_size small (8-16) so arg normalization latency stays low.

If you'd like Redwood to run the dedicated 72-hour pass, we can spin up a provisional pool and provide raw JSONL logs keyed by request_id and a summary dashboard. Costs and required approvals are in the MAP.

Ben Carter
Principal Engineer, Inference Runtime
ben.carter@redwood.ai
